Now you have one minute for your rebuttal.

And I now give the floor to the candidate.
Can I request music?

He needs music, he needs music.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Used with vamos to resume a broadcast or meeting.
Connects a conclusion or agreement.
Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Modifies a verb to mean well or carefully, as in olhar bem (look closely).

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Expresses staying in a place or state (ficar sentado, fica no celular).

examples.text: Ela fica no celular o dia todo.
examples.trans: She stays on her phone all day.

meanings.note: Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.
Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Formal expression of a position, or a street protest.

examples.text: Fica aí a manifestação do candidato.
examples.trans: There stands the statement from the candidate.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Changes -vel to -veis in the plural.

examples.text: Fica a manifestação de um possível presidente.
examples.trans: There stands the statement of a possible president.

meanings.note: Head of state or of an organization.

examples.text: Ele quer ser presidente da república.
examples.trans: He wants to be president of the republic.

meanings.note: Used in presidente da república for the national presidency.

examples.text: Ele é candidato a presidente da república.
examples.trans: He is a candidate for president of the republic.

meanings.note: Marks the current moment resulting from an earlier action.

examples.trans: Now she is in a meeting.

examples.text: Agora tenho que resolver umas coisinhas.
examples.trans: Right now I have to sort out a few little things.

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: Unit of time; um minuto is standard debate timing.
Full form of informal pra; introduces purpose before an infinitive or direction.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

meanings.note: Possessive determiner agreeing with the possessed noun; in Brazil it most often means your (with você).

examples.text: É isso que você quer pra sua vida?
examples.trans: Is that what you want for your life?

meanings.note: In Brazilian debates, the sequence is pergunta (question), resposta (answer), réplica (reply), and tréplica (final rebuttal).

examples.text: Agora tem um minuto para sua tréplica.
examples.trans: Now you have one minute for your rebuttal.

meanings.note: Acabou o seu tempo is the standard phrase for 'Your time is up.'
Refers to someone's time or duration (esse tempo inteiro).

examples.text: Seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?
I stayed there that whole time.

meanings.note: Literally 'obliged'; men say obrigado and women say obrigada.

examples.trans: Thank you very much, you hear?

meanings.note: Expresses duration (por uma hora) and fixed phrases like por exemplo.

examples.trans: I stayed there for an hour.

meanings.note: Formal thanks in broadcasts and offices: obrigado pela colaboração.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your cooperation.
I appreciate the cooperation of everyone.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Passar impune means to go unpunished; passar por means to undergo.

examples.text: Eles passam por muitos testes lá.
examples.trans: They go through many tests there.

meanings.note: In debates and meetings, passar a palavra means to yield or give the floor.

examples.text: Eu passo a palavra agora ao candidato.
examples.trans: I now give the floor to the candidate.

meanings.note: Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.
Used both as a noun and as a formal vocative title in political debates.

examples.text: Eu passo a palavra ao candidato.
examples.trans: I give the floor to the candidate.

examples.text: Candidato, o senhor tem um minuto.

poder.gloss: can; may; to be able to

meanings.en: can; may; to be able to
meanings.note: Core modal verb followed by an infinitive.

examples.text: O senhor pode ser meu fiador?
examples.trans: Can you be my guarantor, sir?

meanings.note: Used for ordering food or requesting an Uber.

examples.trans: I am going to order my ride now.

meanings.note: Both music in general and an individual song.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Spelled with a circumflex when stressed at the end of a phrase or alone (É o quê? / Por quê?).
Third-person masculine singular subject pronoun.
Takes de before a noun (precisa da ajuda) and links directly to an infinitive (precisava gritar).

examples.text: Ela precisa da ajuda do colega.

examples.trans: Did you need to shout at me?

meanings.note: In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.
In the farewell até logo it anticipates meeting again. This is the time adverb, not a short form for a company logo.

examples.trans: I’ll go to the meeting soon.
